learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how computers understand data through 0s and 1s, convert between number systems, and encode human text into computer language!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: We use the Decimal system (base 10: 0-9). Computers use the Binary system (base 2: 0 and 1). Other systems include Octal (base 8) and Hexadecimal (base 16: 0-9 and A-F).
You can convert numbers from one base to another. For example, to convert Decimal to Binary, you repeatedly divide the number by 2 and record the remainders.
Computers only understand numbers (binary). Encoding schemes assign a unique binary number to every letter, number, and symbol on your keyboard so the computer can process text.
ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange) is a common standard for English characters. ISCII is used for Indian language scripts.
Unicode is a universal encoding standard that can represent characters from almost all the written languages in the world (including emojis!), solving the limitations of ASCII.

fun_activity.title: 🔢 Your Name in Binary
fun_activity.instructions: Look up an ASCII to Binary chart online. Try writing your first name entirely in 1s and 0s using the binary codes for each letter!

exam_tips: 📌 Practice converting Decimal to Binary and Binary to Decimal—these are guaranteed exam questions.
📌 Remember the base numbers: Binary (2), Octal (8), Decimal (10), Hexadecimal (16).
📌 Understand that Unicode was created to support multiple global languages, whereas ASCII primarily supports English.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Hexadecimal system uses letters A to F to represent numbers 10 to 15.
⭐ A Bit is a single binary digit (0 or 1), and a Byte is a group of 8 bits.
⭐ UTF-8 is the most popular encoding form of Unicode used on the web today.
